parts.title: My cousin's wedding
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, I went to my cousin Marta's wedding in a small village in Poland. I had never been to such a big wedding before. There were more than two hundred guests, and the party lasted for three days!

The ceremony was in an old church on a hill. Marta looked beautiful in a white dress that her grandmother had made. I was supposed to carry the rings, but I was so nervous that I dropped one on the floor. Everybody laughed, including the priest, and the bride's father found the ring under a chair.

After that, we all walked to a big tent in a field, where the food was waiting. I had never seen so many dishes. The tradition is that the guests keep eating until the early morning, and I thought that I would never feel hungry again.

The next day, there were games for the children and a long walk for the adults. I made friends with a boy called Jakub, and we are still in touch. I would love to go to another Polish wedding one day, but next time I will let somebody else carry the rings.

questions.prompt: What was unusual about the wedding?
options: It was held in a big hotel
Only very close friends came along
Only two guests came from abroad
The party lasted for three days
questions.explanation: There were two hundred guests and the party lasted three days.

questions.prompt: What did the writer do in the church?
options: Read a poem to the bride
Sang a song with the priest
Made a long speech to everyone
questions.explanation: He dropped one of the rings on the floor.

questions.prompt: Who made the wedding dress?
questions.explanation: It was a dress that her grandmother had made.

questions.prompt: What was the tradition at the tent?
options: Guests keep eating until the morning
Everybody dances together in a circle
The bride gives a very long speech
Everybody sings an old song at midnight
questions.explanation: The guests keep eating until the early morning.

questions.prompt: What would the writer do next time?
options: Stay at home with all of his family
Bring a camera with him to take photos
Ask somebody else to carry the rings
questions.explanation: Next time, he will let somebody else carry the rings.

parts.title: Birthday traditions around the world
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
People all over the world celebrate birthdays, but the traditions are very different. [1] A cake with candles is the best-known custom in many countries.

In China, people eat long noodles on their birthday. [2] This is because long noodles mean a long life, and the guest of honour must not cut them.

In Mexico, children often hit a paper animal filled with sweets. [3] When it breaks, all the guests rush to pick up the sweets from the floor.

In Denmark, a flag is put outside the window of the person whose birthday it is. [4] Neighbours can then see it from the street and may call in to say hello.

In some countries, people pull a child's ears once for every year of their age. [5] It sounds painful, but most children say that it is quite gentle, and they are happy to do it.
sentences: In India, friends give the birthday child a small gift of sweets.
It is a cheerful way of showing that there is a celebration at home.
Some customs are known almost everywhere, and others belong to one country.
This is why nobody in Denmark forgets a friend's birthday.
It is a way of wishing the child good luck for the next year.
In the United Kingdom, this game is called "bumps".
The adults hang it from a tree, and the children hit it with a stick.
Eating them is thought to bring good fortune.

gaps.explanation: The traditions are different: some are known almost everywhere, like the cake with candles in the next sentence.
Eating the noodles is thought to bring good fortune, and the next sentence explains why.
The paper animal hangs from a tree and the children hit it; "when it breaks" follows.
A flag is a cheerful way of showing a celebration at home, so neighbours can see it.
Pulling ears is a way of wishing luck, and the next sentence says it sounds painful.

parts.title: A surprise party
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Last month, my brother and I organised a surprise party for our dad's fiftieth birthday. It was not easy to keep it secret [1] him. We told him that we were going out for dinner at a restaurant, but we took him [2] a friend's house instead. All his friends were waiting inside, hiding behind the sofa. When he opened the door, everybody shouted "Surprise!" and he nearly fell [3] with shock. He said that it was the best present he had ever had. We had also made a big cake, [4] had fifty candles on it, and we sang his favourite song. My mother cried a bit, and she told us that she [5] never seen him so happy. In the end, the neighbours came to ask us to be quiet, but they stayed [6] two hours and had some cake.

gaps.explanation: Keep it secret from him: the fixed preposition.
Took him to a friend's house: the direction.
Nearly fell over with shock: phrasal verb.
A cake which had fifty candles: a relative pronoun for a thing.
She had never seen him so happy: past perfect.
Stayed for two hours: a period of time.

parts.title: A talk about wedding planning
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Hello, everybody. I am Alma, and I plan weddings for a living. Today I would like to give you some advice. First, start early. A good wedding needs about a year of preparation. Some people tell me six months is enough, and others plan for two years, but twelve months is just right, because the best places are booked early. Next, the guests. The average wedding in this country has about one hundred guests, but I think that’s too many. You will not talk to everyone, and the cost grows quickly. In my opinion fifty is better, and the day feels warmer. I did a wedding with two hundred once and the couple were exhausted. Now, the place. Many couples think a hotel is the best choice, but a garden is cheaper, and prettier. You only need some tables and good weather, of course. Always have a plan B, like a tent. Some couples dream of a beach, but it’s difficult to arrange. The next question is money. Everybody believes that the dress or the flowers are the biggest cost, but it is the food. It’s more than a third of the budget, so choose carefully. The music is cheaper than people expect, and a friend with a good playlist is enough. Finally, the day itself. Please do not try to organise everything yourself. Give the job of being in charge to a friend. Not your mother, who will be busy with the family, and not the best man, who will have to make a speech. A calm friend who likes lists is perfect. If you follow these ideas, your wedding will be a happy day for everybody, including you. Thank you for listening, and good luck!

gaps.prompt: The best time for preparation is ___
gaps.explanation: Six months is too short and two years too long; twelve months, one year, is just right.

gaps.prompt: The usual number of guests is ___
gaps.explanation: The average wedding has about one hundred guests; two hundred was one special case.

gaps.prompt: Alma prefers a guest list of ___ people
gaps.explanation: In her opinion fifty is better than one hundred.

gaps.prompt: Cheaper place than a hotel: a ___
gaps.explanation: A garden is cheaper than a hotel; a beach is difficult to arrange.

gaps.prompt: The largest part of the budget goes on ___
gaps.explanation: People believe the dress or the flowers cost most, but it is the food.

gaps.prompt: On the day, a ___ should be in charge
gaps.explanation: Not the mother or the best man, but a calm friend should be in charge.

parts.title: An interview with a wedding photographer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Aiden, how did you become a wedding photographer?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People think I studied at a famous school, but I didn’t, and I never worked with my father, he’s an accountant. It started at my uncle’s wedding. I was seventeen, I had an old camera, and the official photographer didn’t arrive. I took all the pictures, and everyone loved them.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What’s the hardest part of your job?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I get tired, the days are long, sometimes twelve hours, but I’m used to that. And the equipment is expensive, though I bought it slowly. The real enemy is the weather. If it rains, the light is dark, the dress gets wet and the couple get upset. I always check the forecast ten times.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Why do people prefer natural photos?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Honestly, the natural ones are the ones that people put on the wall. A grandmother laughing, the groom crying a little when the bride arrives. Posed pictures of the couple are nice, and everybody wants the cake, but those are not the favourites. It’s not that natural photos are easier, they take patience. People choose them because they bring back the real emotion.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you remember a funny moment?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Yes! In a small church, a dog walked in, took the groom’s shoe from beside the door and ran outside. Nobody fell over and the bride kept her ring, thank goodness. I was so amused that I nearly dropped the camera. In the end the dog sat for the family photo.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is there a part of the job that you would change if you could?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Not really. I know it sounds strange, but I love working on Saturdays, even when my friends are out having fun, because I am always part of somebody’s best day. I just wish I had more time to see my own family at weekends.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice do you give for portraits?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Bright colours look great on holiday, but not necessarily on the day, so I don’t ask for them. And please don’t bring twenty friends to the portrait session. What helps is a quiet place, just the couple and me. They relax and they forget the camera.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Why do you want to teach?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I’d love to teach a photography class. I don’t need a large studio, my car is my studio, and I’m not planning to write a travel book. I won’t stop taking photos either, of course. I like the idea because I remember how confusing it was when I started, and I’d like to help beginners avoid my mistakes.
